source: Fedorovich, Gibbs & Shapiro (2017), J. Atmos. Sci. 74, 2813-2834, doi:10.1175/JAS-D-17-0013.1, case B13 (DNS, slope-following frame, dx = 4 m, nu = 1 m2/s).
how_obtained: Read by eye from Figs. 10a, 11a,c, 12a and 13a and from the text of section 5b. Not digitised: treat as +- one contour interval / +- 50 m / +- 0.5 h.

jet_time_h.note: Fig. 12a: strongest 9-11.5 h; text: jet developed by 39600 s

tke_collapse_h.note: Fig. 10a/text: TKE drops to very low values within ~1 h after sunset (3 h)

tke_reemergence_h.note: Fig. 10a/text: turbulence re-emerges ~8 h after sunset, remixing 39600-46800 s

u_over_Vg_250m_sunset.note: Fig. 13a/11c: upslope mixed-layer u at sunset

max_edge_minus_interior_v_over_Vg.note: not from the paper: the boundary-contamination check, ideally << 0.1

qualitative: Daytime CBL (TKE) reaches ~1000 m by 3 h (Fig. 10a).
After the jet collapse at ~11.5-12 h a weaker elevated jet remains near 600 m (46800 s), fading towards 15 h.
The re-emerged turbulent layer is 600-700 m deep from 12 to 15 h.
The flat twin B11 (alpha = 0) does NOT remix: the jet survives the night (Fig. 14a).
